items.name: narration_en
items.direction: Narrate this for a premium documentary YouTube Shorts channel about money, history and the tricks behind them. The Narrator is a deep, warm, confident storyteller with a hint of mystery: curious, quietly amused, energetic and punchy, never slow, never announcer-like. Natural emphasis on dates and numbers, questions end with a curious lift, a short comic pause before each punchline. Keep the same voice, pace and energy from start to finish.
lines: Narrator
This note says one hundred trillion dollars. On its first day, it was worth about thirty dollars.
Narrator
How do you get there? In November two thousand eight, prices in Zimbabwe were rising about ninety-eight percent a day.
Narrator
They doubled roughly every twenty-five hours. Monthly inflation hit an estimated seventy-nine point six billion percent.
Narrator
The government kept cutting zeros off the money. Twenty-five of them, in three rounds.
Narrator
Then, in April two thousand nine, it gave up. People switched to US dollars and rand.
Narrator
In twenty fifteen, the old money was finally swapped: one US dollar for thirty-five quadrillion Zimbabwe dollars.
Narrator
Your hundred trillion note? About forty cents.
Narrator
Here's the twist: collectors now pay around a hundred dollars for one.
Narrator
That's the mirage: a number on paper isn't wealth. Money is only worth what people trust.
Narrator
This is Money Mirage. Follow for more.
